candidate.answerReason: A positive integer has an odd number of positive divisors exactly when it is a perfect square. There are seven positive squares below 50.

methods.label: Pair the divisors
methods.explanation:
Divisors naturally come in factor pairs. For a positive integer \(n\), pair each positive divisor \(d\) with \(n/d\). Pairing again returns \(d\), so the distinct divisors are grouped into pairs unless the two members coincide.

They coincide exactly when
\[
d=\frac nd,
\qquad d^2=n.
\]
Thus a nonsquare has an even number of divisors. A square has one unpaired divisor, \(\sqrt n\), and all its other divisors occur in pairs, giving an odd total. This also includes \(1\), whose only divisor is \(1\).

Since \(7^2=49<50<64=8^2\), the eligible integers are
\[
1,4,9,16,25,36,49.
\]
There are \(7\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
methods.levelReason: Factor pairing proves the result with elementary divisibility and parity, without prime factorization.
